vaccine.title: Paris bans smallpox inoculation
vaccine.line: Amid a smallpox outbreak some blamed on inoculation, the Paris Parlement banned the practice in the city until doctors and theologians ruled.

vaccine.title: Marblehead burns its smallpox hospital
vaccine.line: Fearing a new private inoculation hospital would spread smallpox and scare off ships, Marblehead townspeople sneaked onto its island and burned it.

springtime.title: The Ionian Revolt against Persia
springtime.line: Miletus’s leader ousted Persian-backed tyrants across Ionia, and the revolt leapt to Caria, Byzantium and Cyprus, according to Herodotus, the main source.

springtime.title: Europe’s wave of revolts, 1378 to 1382
springtime.line: Within five years, worker, peasant and tax revolts erupted in Florence, Ghent, England, Rouen and Paris, as news passed between them.

phone.title: Morse’s telegraph sends its first message
phone.line: Samuel Morse tapped “What hath God wrought” from Washington to Baltimore; within 17 years wires spanned the continent, carrying news in minutes.

yellow.title: Song China’s “small papers” spread fabrications
yellow.line: Song officials warned that xiaobao, popular private news sheets, invented imperial orders and appointments out of nothing and spread them widely.

titanic.title: The White Ship sinks off Normandy
titanic.line: Nobles partying aboard the newly refitted White Ship pushed it to overtake the king’s vessel; it hit a rock, drowning his heir.

weimar.title: Rome’s debased coins and Diocletian’s price edict
weimar.line: Emperors debased Rome’s silver coins to pay soldiers until prices soared; Diocletian’s edict capped prices on pain of death, but largely failed.

weimar.title: The Jin dynasty prints notes without limit
weimar.line: Fighting the Mongols, northern China’s Jin dynasty printed notes without limit; by 1214 it issued 1,000-string notes, and people turned to silver.

weimar.title: Delhi’s token currency collapses
weimar.line: Sultan Muhammad bin Tughluq issued brass and copper tokens valued as silver; people forged them at home until the coins were worthless.

weimar.title: Revolutionary France’s assignats collapse
weimar.line: Revolutionary France printed about 45 billion livres in assignats to pay debts and wars; by 1796 they were nearly worthless.

dust.title: The dim sun after Caesar’s murder
dust.line: Amid turmoil after Caesar’s murder, Romans described a darkened sun; eruptions of Etna and Alaska’s Okmok brought cold, failed harvests and famine.

dust.title: New England’s Dark Day
dust.line: Smoke, likely from Canadian wildfires in a drought year, darkened New England at midday during the Revolutionary War; many feared Judgment Day.

transistor.title: Cai Lun improves papermaking
transistor.line: Cai Lun, head of the Han palace workshop, presented an improved papermaking method using bark, rags and fishnets; paper later spread worldwide.

transistor.title: China records the first gunpowder formulas
transistor.line: Chinese alchemists seeking an elixir of life likely stumbled on gunpowder; its first formulas date to 1044, and it remade warfare worldwide.

transistor.title: Gutenberg’s printing press
transistor.line: Goldsmith Johannes Gutenberg developed a movable-type press; by 1500, presses in about 270 European cities had printed over 20 million copies.

springs.title: Guru Jambheshwar founds the Bishnoi community
springs.line: In Rajasthan, Guru Jambheshwar founded the Bishnoi community, whose 29 rules forbid felling green trees and killing animals; followers still protect wildlife.

dolly.title: Aldini tries to revive a corpse
dolly.line: In London, Giovanni Aldini electrified a hanged murderer’s corpse; the jaw quivered, an eye opened, and onlookers thought the man might revive.
